raw_response:
I will put all 7.0 mu into cotton again this year, because that is the crop I know best and I have grown it for many years. At my age, with only two people in the household and some labor going off-farm, I will keep the plan simple and steady rather than complicated. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on that to protect emergence and support flowering and boll setting, but I will not over-irrigate because that raises cost and can push too much vegetative growth. I will use improved seed instead of traditional seed because I want better stand establishment, more uniform growth, and more stable yield. For fertilization, I will apply a moderate rate of nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium together, because cotton on my land needs balanced feeding, not just nitrogen. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on a 7.0 mu farm and it fits my labor situation. I will spray pesticides several times during the season, mainly to control the common insects and diseases when pressure rises, but I will keep it to a practical number to control cost. My goal is a stable yield, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than chasing the highest possible output.
